title: Siegard captured run
description: What one run of the caller's commands did: written by `bin/run.py` at `run/<slug>/run.json` under the delivery root, beside the logs the commands printed. It is material, not a node — the delivery validator keeps it and never validates it, the way a work root keeps `intake/` — and a review points at the directory rather than restating what is in it. There is no timestamp, no duration and no record of the environment: two runs of the same commands over the same tree produce records that differ only where the commands did, and a record that changes on its own could not be compared with another. There is no count of tests either, passing or failing: counting them means parsing a reporter's format, which is knowledge of a stack that neither this contract nor the script that writes it holds. Whoever diagnoses the failures counts them from the output, and says how many they counted.

run.description: This run's directory under the delivery root, which is also its identity — the caller named it, and nothing here was minted from a clock.

cwd.description: The directory the commands ran in, resolved. A run says where it happened, because the same command in two trees is two runs.

timeout_seconds.description: The bound the caller set, recorded with the run it bounded. No value is shipped: a number this framework supplied would be one nobody calibrated, and a step recorded as timed out is only readable against the bound it exceeded.

outcome.description: How the run ended: the outcome of the first step that did not pass, or `passed` when every step did. Never absent and never `not_run` — a record exists because a run happened.

failed_step.description: The name of the first step that did not pass, or null. Null with an outcome other than `passed` is a contradiction; the two are written together and read together.

name.description: The caller's name for this step. Unique within the run: one step, one outcome.

command.description: The argument vector that was executed, joined for a reader. No shell saw it, so nothing in it expanded.

outcome.description: `not_run` means a step before this one did not pass and this one was never attempted — never that it was skipped for any other reason. A suite run against a tree that did not compile would report failures about a binary nobody built, so a failed step stops the run.

exit_code.description: What the command exited with, or null where it never exited — timed out, was not found, or was never attempted.

output.description: The log holding everything this step printed, relative to the run's own directory; null where the step was never attempted. Byte-exact: what a diagnosis reads is what the command wrote.

combined_output.description: The log holding every step's output in order, each under a header naming the step, its command and its outcome — relative to the run's own directory. It is the file a diagnosis reads in full; the per-step logs stay byte-exact beside it.
